newsitem.title: USA: Rev. Jackson says Texaco boycott threat still on.
newsitem.headline: Rev. Jackson says Texaco boycott threat still on.

text.p: Black civil rights leader Rev. Jesse Jackson said Friday that his threat to start a boycott Saturday against Texaco Inc still stood, although Texaco had reached a settlement in a race bias suit brought by six African American employees.
"At this point it's still very much a threat," Jackson said in an interview on CNN.
Jackson said he would talk to other civil rights leaders Saturday night to decide what steps to take following the announcement of the settlement.

He said in addition to employment discrimination, settled in the suit, civil rights leaders were concerned about "lack of business opportunities, joint ventures and professional services" opportunities for minorities.
"We do not yet have a major complete package," Jackson said. He met earlier this week with Texaco Chairman Peter Bijur urging him to set out a plan to address all the minority groups' concerns.
Jackson said Bijur told him Friday that he would have a more comprehensive plan to address those concerns "within the next few days."
